Neonatal intraventricular haemorrhage. Plasma volume expansion in preterm neonates has been thought to help prevent neonatal intraventricular haemorrhage (p.1050). However, a study using plasma or gelatin as plasma volume expanders,1,2 found no evidence of a decreased risk of such haemorrhage or subsequent death or disability. 1. Plasma exchange. Therapeutic plasma exchange or plas- mapheresis are procedures in which plasma is selectively re- moved from the body while the cellular constituents of blood are retained. Although the two terms are commonly used synony- mously, plasmapheresis generally involves the removal of small volumes of plasma, whereas plasma exchange removes larger volumes which must be replaced with a suitable fluid.
